about_long:
I'm a software engineer in Vienna with a mathematics background. I joined Erste Digital, Erste Group's technology subsidiary, as an intern in February 2024 and have been a Software Engineer there since September 2024. I lead an internal AI accelerator team whose pipeline turns legacy Natural/Adabas mainframe code into as-is documentation, generated Java/OSB integration connectors and review-ready pull requests. Static analysis, generated tests, code-vs-documentation checks and mandatory human review are built in. So far it has delivered five complete use cases and 10+ connectors and cut typical use-case cycle time by over 80%. I also maintain customer-data services and own production incidents in a regulated banking environment.

I completed my BSc in Mathematics at the University of Vienna in the standard six semesters while working. My thesis, written within the Bachelor seminar and graded 1, built quantum neural networks in Qiskit and PyTorch for financial forecasting, with a reproducible pipeline benchmarked on 121 held-out days against classical baselines. I'm now in the MSc, focusing on martingale optimal transport and model calibration. At WUTIS, a Vienna student investment society, I led two project teams and ran coding workshops.

Outside work I build research systems. Pulse, my solo crypto-perpetuals stack, runs 24/7 on a Raspberry Pi 5. Its daily market-neutral book reached a Sharpe ratio of 3.45 on a one-look 2026 holdout (backtest), results are deflated for the full count of about 1,900 variants tried, and it is written up as a working paper.

I built Pulse and two LLM projects, a prediction-market contract matcher and an n8n agent stack, with AI coding agents (Claude Code and Codex); in Pulse, adversarial verifier agents rebuilt results from raw data.

bullets: Lead an internal AI accelerator team and built an AI modernization pipeline for legacy Natural/Adabas mainframe code: call-chain mapping → source ingestion → AI analysis and as-is documentation (screens, business rules) → generated Java/OSB integration connectors → review-ready pull requests.
Delivered 5 complete use cases and 10+ connectors; typical use-case cycle time fell by over 80%, from more than three monthly release cycles to under one work week and a single release (n = 5).

Orchestrate Copilot CLI, Bash, a deterministic code transpiler, MCP, agents and reusable skills in CI/CD, with quality gates from static analysis, generated tests, code-vs-documentation checks and mandatory human review.

Maintain customer-data services, the OSB–Natural integration layer and data-delivery endpoints; introduced Kafka lifecycle events (mainframe to Kafka) for traceability and monitoring; own production incidents in a regulated banking environment.

research.title: Alpha search in crypto perpetual futures
research.kind: Working paper, short public edition (10 pages, not peer-reviewed)
research.summary: A search, July to October 2026, for an edge in crypto perpetual futures that survives realistic costs. About 1,900 variants were tried (1,871 counted by 21 October, about 1,700 of them a written estimate of the unlogged July–August search), and the results were deflated for that full count. From 12 October, new tests were pre-registered in a hash-chained ledger. Methods include holdouts opened once, walk-forward tests, combinatorial purged cross-validation (CPCV) with embargo, HAC t-statistics, the deflated Sharpe ratio, PBO and placebo and label-permutation controls. The cost-aware tests rejected most candidate families, and one low-turnover, dollar-neutral cross-sectional book passed its single look at a 2026 holdout: +23.0 bp/day net of costs and funding, HAC t 2.61, Sharpe ratio 3.45, worst drawdown 7.9% (backtest). A simulation on a fixed $500 from January 2023 to September 2026 made +$1,124 on Bybit data and +$1,144 on Binance data after fees, slippage and funding. Backtest and simulation only; not investment advice.

research.title: Quantum Neural Networks: Theory and Application for Financial Time Series Forecasting
research.kind: BSc thesis, University of Vienna (written within the Bachelor seminar, graded 1)
research.summary: Bachelor thesis in mathematics, supervised by Priv.-Doz. Dr. Lukas Exl. It builds quantum neural networks in Qiskit, tunes them with Optuna and retrains them under simulated gate noise to forecast the returns and covariances of five assets; the case study grew out of a WUTIS team project I led. The pipeline is benchmarked on a 121-day held-out test window against classical baselines, and the thesis was graded 1.

research.title: Bass local-volatility model on SPX options: a replication of Conze and Henry-Labordère (2021)
research.kind: Paper replication, MSc summer research project
research.summary: Summer 2026 research project with Prof. Julio Backhoff-Veraguas, implementing “Bass Construction with Multi-Marginals: Lightspeed Computation in a New Local Volatility Model” on a public SPX option-chain sample: forward normalisation from put–call parity, OTM quotes to marginals, fixed-point calibration, Asian and forward-start repricing, the local-vol representation, vol Greeks and vanilla (vega) hedges, and the Bass2 general-kernel operator (Theorem 6.1), checked against the Brownian case; the future-skew and stochastic-volatility calibrations (Sections 6.2–6.3) were not implemented. Replacing 24-node Gauss–Hermite quadrature with an exact convolution of the piecewise-linear maps restores the martingale property (max |z| 17.8 → 1.8) and cuts the fixed point from 254/499 to 10/12 iterations. A faithful replication for research, not a production pricer.
